extracted.intended_audience: aspiring late-night television comedy writers submitting packets
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for assembling and polishing a writing packet (professional portfolio) to submit to the head writer of a late-night TV show. Focuses on topicality, voice, uniqueness, distinctiveness, and mechanical correctness to increase hiring chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the jokes up-to-date
rubrics_metrics.description: Late-night monologues are all about the day’s news, so yours should be as current as possible. “Let’s say your packet is due on Friday... I would only write jokes about things that happened on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target very recent events — monologue material should reflect the immediate news cycle. Avoid stale or older topical jokes; freshness is critical because monologues respond to the day's headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the voice of the host you’re pitching
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you pitch, do your homework and watch enough episodes to know the voice you’re writing for. Don’t submit material that doesn’t fit the host (e.g., an incongruent big musical number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor tone, format, and types of jokes to the particular host and show. Watch episodes to learn what the host does and does not do; submitting off-brand pieces signals you haven't seen the show and reduces your chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring your uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Show what you—and only you—can bring to the show that they are not already doing. Fresh, unique material makes the staff think, ‘We wish this person worked here right now so we could put this on the show tonight.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize distinctive perspectives, experiences, or skills (example: a writer with fraud-protection experience offering specific angles on related political stories). Unique angles increase hireability; avoid generic or redundant material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make your jokes stand out
rubrics_metrics.description: Because your packet will be stacked among hundreds of submissions, think about how to push further and find something more surprising and unique rather than obvious jokes that many others will also submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek surprising, uncommon takes rather than obvious punches (e.g., avoid joke angles likely duplicated across many packets). Consider risk/edge that still fits the show's voice to differentiate your material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean it up (mechanical accuracy and fact-checking)
rubrics_metrics.description: The humor may be dirty, but the copy should not be. Spelling, grammar or factual errors can instantly propel your work down that 300-pile stack. Errors indicate lack of work ethic or meticulousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread carefully, check facts, and ensure correct grammar/spelling. The head writer's reputation is on the line when passing along packets — don’t give reasons to be placed in the ‘Maybe’ pile. Review every single word.
